newsitem.title: ITALY: Scuffles as trial of Venice belltower resumes.
newsitem.headline: Scuffles as trial of Venice belltower resumes.

text.p: Police fired teargas to disperse left-wing demonstrators who jostled businessmen and politicians as the trial resumed on Tuesday of eight men who occupied the St Mark's belltower in Venice, eyewitnesses said.
One man was taken to hospital after being hit on the head.

Around 100 demonstrators shouted slogans and hurled objects at sympathisers of a group called the Free Federalist Entrepreneurs of Europe (LIFE) as they entered the court building in Mestre, just outside the lagoon city.

The LIFE group, which accuses the Rome government of smothering business with high taxes, has raised funds to pay for a legal defence for the eight men who stormed the belltower in a separatist stunt in the early hours of May 8.
The demonstrators hurled insults, calling those associated with LIFE "petty businessmen and tax evaders."
Marco Taradash, a member of parliament of the right-wing Forza Italia party and the leader of LIFE, Fabio Padovan, were pushed, kicked and spat at as they entered the court building.
Franco Rocchetta, a leader of the Venetian League, which advocates a separate Northeast Italian state, was struck on the head outside the courtroom and taken to hospital.

The eight, who hijacked a ferry in the early hours of May 9 to take them and a home-made armoured vehicle down the Grand Canal to St Mark's, were arrested when police stormed the landmark and ended the brief sit-in.
The men, who could be jailed for up to 25 years if convicted, face charges ranging from illegal arms possession, threatening public officials, kidnapping and occupying church property.
They issued a statement before their arrest declaring themselves soldiers of the "Most Serene Republic" of Venice, for centuries a maritime power before its fall 200 years ago.
Judge Graziana Campanato, presiding over the Assize Court, on Tuesday threw out a plea from lawyers representing two defendants for more time to prepare their defence.

She also rejected a request from the defence for the trial to be conducted under a special fast-track procedure, which would allow for a reduced sentence if there is a conviction, after prosecutor Rita Ugolini raised objections.
